$comment: SHARED CROSS-SOURCE FIXTURE — the OVPN 'unresolvable external file reference' rule.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Two implementations enforce this rule: A3's Swift parse-time reject
findUnresolvableOpenvpnFileReferences). They were built to the same stated rule and reported to agree
'by construction'. They did not. A line-by-line diff on 2026-09-08 found three divergences, two of
which were silent bypasses in the Swift side (tab separator, '--' prefix). Two implementations in two
languages never agree by construction — they agree until they drift, and nothing was measuring it.
THIS FILE IS THE MEASUREMENT. Both suites read these rows. A drift on EITHER side reds BOTH.
Add a row here, never only in one language's tests — a case that exists in one suite is exactly the
THE RULE. A directive in inline_required_directives is an UNRESOLVABLE FILE REFERENCE when a
non-comment line's FIRST TOKEN equals it (after stripping a leading '--' of >=3 chars) AND the line has
>=2 tokens AND no '<directive>' inline block appears anywhere in the blob. Tokens split on space OR tab.
Lines split on LF, CRLF or lone CR. Comments are '#' and ';'. Comparison is CASE-SENSITIVE.
WHY IT MATTERS. The node renders the blob into an isolated directory containing only client.ovpn and
auth.txt, so a referenced file will not exist and openvpn dies with an error naming neither the field
nor the cause. That silent class is what this rule guards. A config openvpn rejects at OPTION-PARSE
time instead fails loudly with a line number and is NOT this class — see failure_class per row.

evidence.method: ran /opt/homebrew/sbin/openvpn --config <blob> --verb 0 and read the option parser's verdict
case_sensitivity: <ca> ... </ca>  -> parsed OK (proceeds to 'No client-side authentication method is specified')
<CA> ... </CA>  -> 'Options error: Unrecognized option or missing or extra parameter(s) ...: CA'
CA ca.crt       -> 'Options error: Unrecognized option ...: CA'
evidence.conclusion: openvpn is case-sensitive for BOTH the inline tag and the keyword. Uppercase forms are rejected by openvpn's own parser with a line number, i.e. they fail LOUD, which is a different class from the silent unresolvable-file failure this rule guards.

base:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194

cases.name: inline_ca_block_is_self_contained
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
<ca>
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
AAAA
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
</ca>
cases.why: the normal provider shape; flagging it would reject working configs

cases.name: bare_ca_file_reference
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
ca ca.crt
cases.why: points at a file the node's isolated dir will not contain

cases.name: bare_cert_file_reference
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
cert client.crt

cases.name: crlf_config_must_still_split
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
remote vpn.example.com 1194
ca ca.crt
cases.why: most .ovpn files are Windows-authored. Swift treats \r\n as ONE Character, so split(separator:"\n") does not split them at all — that exact defect already shipped once in this parser

cases.name: lone_cr_classic_mac_line_endings
cases.blob: clientdev tunremote vpn.example.com 1194ca ca.crt
cases.why: what a truncated CRLF write also leaves behind

cases.name: hash_commented_reference_is_inert
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
# ca ca.crt

cases.name: semicolon_commented_reference_is_inert
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
; ca ca.crt

cases.name: inline_block_wins_over_stray_file_line
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
ca ca.crt
<ca>
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
AAAA
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
</ca>
cases.why: openvpn uses the inline block and the stray line is inert; flagging this rejects valid provider configs — the expensive direction, because a gate that rejects valid input gets disabled

cases.name: bare_directive_without_argument
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
ca
cases.why: no file argument, so it is not a reference

cases.name: tab_separated_reference_W3098
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
ca	ca.crt
cases.why: SILENT BYPASS #1 in the Swift side: it split on the space literal, so this was one token and was accepted. openvpn's config lexer separates on space AND tab.

cases.name: tab_separated_tls_auth_with_direction_arg
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
tls-auth	ta.key 0
cases.why: hyphenated directive plus a trailing direction argument, tab-separated

cases.name: double_dash_prefixed_reference_W3098
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
--ca ca.crt
cases.why: SILENT BYPASS #2: openvpn strips a leading '--' from a config-file directive, so this is honoured as 'ca ca.crt'. Unnormalised, the whole rule was a two-character bypass.

cases.name: tab_padded_bare_directive_negative_control
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
ca
cases.why: NEGATIVE CONTROL for the tab widening — still no file argument

cases.name: inline_wins_after_double_dash_normalisation
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
--ca ca.crt
<ca>
AAAA
</ca>
cases.why: NEGATIVE CONTROL for the '--' widening — inline must still win

cases.name: bare_double_dash_is_not_a_keyword
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
--
cases.why: the '>=3' length guard exists so the bare '--' argument delimiter cannot normalise to an empty keyword

cases.name: prefix_is_not_equality
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
cafile x.crt
cases.why: token EQUALITY, not prefix — 'cafile' is a different directive

cases.name: uppercase_keyword_is_not_our_class
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
CA ca.crt
cases.why: VERIFIED against openvpn 2.7.0: 'CA' is an unrecognised option and openvpn refuses the config at parse time with a line number. It fails LOUD, so it is not the silent class this rule guards. Matching case-insensitively here makes an implementation over-broad and breaks set-equality with the other side.

cases.name: uppercase_inline_tag_does_not_satisfy_the_reference
cases.blob:
client
dev tun
proto udp
remote vpn.example.com 1194
<CA>
AAAA
</CA>
ca ca.crt
cases.why: VERIFIED against openvpn 2.7.0: '<CA>' is NOT recognised as an inline ca block ('Unrecognized option ...: CA'), so the 'ca ca.crt' reference is genuinely unresolved. Rejecting is correct AND the error text ('inline it as a <ca> block') is the right guidance. Note the class is LOUD, not silent — openvpn refuses this config itself — so this row is lower severity than the tab and '--' rows.
